title: The protocol's environment negotiation is a trusted channel into a privileged helper's argv
index_line: T-0044 · AUTH_DECISION · telnet ENVIRON USER becomes `login -f root`; no password is ever asked · c/any-inetd-helper · corroborated
invariant_violated: A remote client's environment is assumed to be advisory data — TERM, DISPLAY, LANG — which the daemon passes to the login program so the session is set up usefully. But the login program's option grammar is in the same argv, so a value that begins with a dash is read as an option, and one of those options is 'this user is already authenticated'.

mechanism.does: the attacker negotiates the protocol's environment option and supplies a variable whose value is an option string plus a user
the daemon assembles the login helper's command line, inserting the client-supplied environment value as an argument
the helper's option parser sees the leading dash and applies the pre-authenticated-user option
the helper's pre-authenticated-user option marks the caller as already authenticated — no password is requested or checked — and a root session is established for a client that never authenticated

source.protocol.value: the protocol's environment/variable negotiation (telnet ENVIRON, RFC 1572) — a pre-auth channel by design

sink.exec.noshell.value: the exec of the privileged login helper; the payload is an argv token, not a metacharacter

encoding.shell.value: `-<flag> <user>` as the environment value; the space is significant and the dash is the entire trick

guard.none.value: the daemon never validates the variable's value, and the helper has no `--` before client-derived arguments

preconditions.expr: a telnet (or equivalent inetd-style) service is reachable and spawns a login helper
the daemon passes the negotiated environment into the helper's argv without filtering dash-prefixed values
the build predates the fixed release (inetutils 2.8)

success: a session is granted with no credential exchange at all — the password prompt never appears
the negotiated variable is visible in the daemon's argv (process listing or audit log)
the resulting shell has the privilege of the requested user, not the connecting one
failure_like: the daemon strips or rejects values containing spaces or leading dashes
the helper is invoked with `--` before client-derived arguments
false_positive: a successful login using real credentials — the tell is that no password was requested
a banner or refused connection proving the port is open — reachability, not bypass

hazards: environment negotiation is the classic forgotten input: TERM/DISPLAY/USER look like metadata and are sent pre-auth by design
the option grammar of the *helper* is what matters; read `login`, `su`, `sshd`-adjacent helpers rather than the daemon
argument injection again, but through an environment variable rather than a URL — the fourth distinct route in this store (see T-0036, T-0039, T-0005)
the two-patch history matters: the first fix filtered one variable, the second applied the same sanitiser to every path
non_transfers: daemons that never hand client environment to a privileged helper
helpers invoked with an explicit option terminator
